Test for differences between two independent groups using SAM

gly_sam.Rd

Apply Significance Analysis of Microarrays (SAM) to glycan or glycopeptide abundances. Positive scores indicate higher mean abundance in the test group on the analysis scale.

Usage

gly_sam(
  exp,
  group_col = "group",
  ref_group = NULL,
  delta = NULL,
  n_perm = 100L,
  s0 = NULL,
  seed = 1L,
  add_info = TRUE,
  log_transform = NULL
)

Arguments

exp

A glyexp::GlycomicSE() or glyexp::GlycoproteomicSE() object, or another SummarizedExperiment containing expression data and sample information.

group_col

A character string specifying the column name in sample information that contains group labels. Default is "group".

ref_group

A character string specifying the reference group. If NULL (default), the first level of the group factor is used as the reference. Only used for two-group comparisons.

delta

A positive threshold or a vector of distinct positive thresholds for the departure of ordered scores from their permutation expectations. The default, NULL, returns the ten grid entries chosen by siggenes::samControl(). Supply one value to call individual features. With a grid, called is NA for every feature.

n_perm

Requested number of label permutations, at least two. Uses all allocations if fewer exist. For more than 30,000 possible allocations, siggenes can draw the same allocation more than once.

s0

Nonnegative regularization constant in analysis units. By default siggenes estimates it across features. This requires at least 25 distinct testable standard errors and variation in the scores used to estimate it. A prespecified value also permits analysis of smaller panels with at least two testable features.

seed

Nonnegative integer seed for the permutations. The caller's random-number state is restored after fitting.

add_info

A logical value. If TRUE (default), variable information from the experiment will be added to the result tibble. If FALSE, only the statistical results are returned.

log_transform

NULL (default) uses metadata(exp)$scale to avoid logging data twice. TRUE requests the method's log transformation for raw data; if the input is already on "log", "log2", "log10", or "logx", it warns and uses the supplied values unchanged. FALSE always uses the supplied values unchanged. This argument must be named when it follows ....

Value

A glystats_sam_res object inheriting from glystats_res. get_tidy_result() returns one row per input feature in assay order.

  • .variable is the SE feature ID (variable for legacy experiments). ref_group and test_group identify the comparison.

  • d is the signed SAM score. p_val is the backend's two-sided p-value from the pooled permuted scores. q_value is its feature q-value computed from those p-values and the estimated null proportion (q.version = 1).

  • called uses the inclusive lower and upper score cutoffs for a single supplied delta. n_finite counts finite observations on the analysis scale. Excluded rows have missing statistics and calls, and an exclusion of "non_finite", "backend_missing_code", or "unestimable_variance".

thresholds has one row per delta, with the lower and upper score cutoffs, number called (n_called), mean number of false calls under permutation (expected_false), estimated null proportion (p0), and the backend's permutation FDR (fdr, a fraction). siggenes reports an FDR of zero when a threshold calls zero features.

diagnostics records the input and tested feature counts, fitted s0, and the numbers of actual and distinct permutations. settings records the requested comparison and tuning parameters. get_raw_result() returns the fitted SAM object. Its feature labels are the original one-based row positions so even long SE identifiers map unambiguously. The result retains the input meta_data, the applied preprocessing and the SE identifiers mapping described in gly_identity.

Details

Supply two groups with at least two independent samples each. The null distribution assumes sample labels are exchangeable and preserves group sizes. Paired, blocked, covariate-adjusted and multigroup designs are unsupported. For blocking or covariate adjustment, see gly_limma().

Install the optional Bioconductor backend with BiocManager::install("siggenes"). Its dependency multtest supplies the observed score components used to check which features are testable.

siggenes::sam() uses the test-minus-reference mean difference divided by the unpooled standard error plus s0 (its two-class Welch statistic). Raw assays use log2(x + 1e-6) by default. For relative abundances, the sign describes a change relative to the normalization reference. With logx, it describes a difference in the supplied coordinates.

Only features with finite values in every sample and estimable within-group variation enter the common permutation distribution. The backend treats numerically zero standard errors as untestable, including features constant within both groups. It also reserves the finite value -93074815 as a missing-data code on the analysis scale. A feature containing that value is excluded before permutation. Filtering is reported, and each excluded feature retains its ID and reason. The p-values, q-values and threshold FDR estimates apply to the retained family. No imputation or fold-change filter is applied.

References

Tusher VG, Tibshirani R, Chu G (2001). Significance analysis of microarrays applied to the ionizing radiation response. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 98, 5116-5121. doi:10.1073/pnas.091062498 .

siggenes on Bioconductor.

Examples

exp <- glyexp::real_experiment2
group <- SummarizedExperiment::colData(exp)$group
two_groups <- exp[, group %in% c("H", "C")]
res <- gly_sam(two_groups, ref_group = "H", delta = 1, seed = 42)
#> Warning: SAM inference uses 29 of 66 features.
#> ℹ All input IDs are retained. See exclusion for the reason each feature was
#>   omitted.
res$thresholds
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   delta cutoff_lower cutoff_upper n_called expected_false    p0   fdr
#>   <dbl>        <dbl>        <dbl>    <int>          <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     1         -Inf         1.31       12           2.43     1 0.202
head(subset(get_tidy_result(res), called, select = c(.variable, d, q_value)))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>   .variable                          d q_value
#>   <chr>                          <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 Hex(5)HexNAc(2)                 1.39   0.425
#> 2 Hex(3)HexNAc(4)dHex(1)          6.03   0    
#> 3 Hex(5)HexNAc(3)NeuAc(1)         1.74   0.376
#> 4 Hex(5)HexNAc(5)dHex(1)          1.46   0.408
#> 5 Hex(5)HexNAc(5)dHex(1)NeuAc(1)  1.31   0.458
#> 6 Hex(3)HexNAc(5)dHex(1)          4.47   0
